title: Graceful capacity fallback and credit emergency proxy
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: During recent production incidents we observed sharp tenant throughput drops when warm pools exhausted and immediate backfill paths were unavailable. This PR implements a lightweight runtime proxy that provides two capabilities: 1) Transparent capacity fallback to degraded-but-compatible model variants or lower-concurrency paths when the preferred pool is constrained; 2) Emergency credit borrowing (short-lived, safety-capped) from a cross-tenant emergency ledger that lets critical requests complete while preserving global SLA budgets. Design summary: the proxy sits in the serving request router and evaluates a candidate request's priority, estimated token cost, and current pool headroom. If headroom < threshold and request is high-priority, the proxy first attempts a local fallback (compatible model variant, quantized path, reduced max_tokens). If local fallback insufficient, it will attempt to borrow emergency credit from the reservation ledger via a bounded API: borrow_credit(tenant_id, amount, ttl, reason). Borrowed credit is tracked and reclaimed by subtracting from the tenant's next commit or through an automatic compensation factor applied over N windows. Safety: credits are strictly capped per-tenant and per-cluster, borrow attempts can be rate-limited and audited. Important configuration knobs live in /configs/fleet/fallback-proxy.yaml and are feature-gated under rollout flag rollout.fallback_proxy.enabled. Implementation notes: - Router changes (router/proxy/fallback_proxy.go): new decision path and lightweight state machine. - Ledger client (ledger/emergency_client.go): borrow/release RPC, local cache with optimistic concurrency. - Metrics and tracing: added metrics fallback_proxy.attempts, fallback_proxy.success, fallback_proxy.credit_borrowed, fallback_proxy.credit_repaid, and traces for decision span. - Policy engine (policy/fallback_policy.json): serialized rules for compatible fallbacks keyed by model_family, sequence_length_profile, and tenant_tier. Backwards compatibility: when rollout flag disabled, router behavior unchanged. Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary fleet -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days with synthetic load tests during each step. Migration: adds a ledger table emergency_credits but maintains existing reservation flows. Testing: unit tests for policy matching and ledger semantics; integration tests in perf-canary that simulate pool exhaustion; chaos tests that kill warm-pool nodes and verify fallback latency and no loss of critical requests. Performance summary (canary results): - median latency for fallback-eligible requests: +12ms (p95 +35ms) vs baseline; - success rate for prioritized requests in exhaustion scenarios improved from 63% to 94%; - emergency-credit utilization peaked at 8% of safety cap during simulated storm. Observability: dashboards added in observability-pack/fallback-proxy.json; alerts: FallbackProxy:HighBorrowRate and FallbackProxy:UnrepaidCredit. Risks and mitigations: - Overuse of emergency credit: capped and auto-repay; alerts created. - Incompatibility with strict tenant isolation: option to disable borrowing per-tenant via tenant config. - Complexity in billing: billing signals are emitted (billing.emergency_credit.used) and will be reconciled in billing pipeline. Related work items: Linear ENG-1538 (fallback routing RFC), ENG-1689 (ledger sharding), PM-4021 (priority tiers).

release_notes: Introduce a fallback proxy that transparently routes requests to degraded-compatible paths and a bounded emergency credit mechanism for critical request preservation during warm-pool exhaustion. Configurable via rollout.fallback_proxy.enabled and fleet fallback config. Observability and billing hooks included.
notes: Deployed to canary on 2026-02-17, rolled to 5% on 2026-02-18 after green metrics, 25% on 2026-02-19 with synthetic load, and 100% on 2026-02-20. No customer-facing regressions observed; one billing reconciliation edge case fixed on 2026-02-19.
qa_summary: QA validated policy matching, borrow/release semantics, and repayment behavior. Chaos test killed warm nodes and verified prioritized requests were preserved. Load test validated p95 latency impact within SLA for non-fallback traffic.
